:::{#exm-equivalence-iff}
#### A tautological biconditional
<!-- no-figure: the truth table is the display -->

@exm-logically-equivalent showed that
$P \Rightarrow Q$ and $\neg P \lor Q$ are [logically equivalent](#def-logically-equivalent).
Adding a column for the biconditional to its [truth table](#def-truth-table)
gives:

| $P$ | $Q$ | $\neg P \lor Q$ | $P \Rightarrow Q$ | $(P \Rightarrow Q) \Leftrightarrow (\neg P \lor Q)$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---------------:|:-----------------:|:---------------------------------------------------:|
| T   | T   | T               | T                 | T                                                   |
| T   | F   | F               | F                 | T                                                   |
| F   | T   | T               | T                 | T                                                   |
| F   | F   | T               | T                 | T                                                   |

The last column is true in every row,
so the biconditional is a [tautology](#def-tautology),
as [equivalence as a tautological biconditional](#thm-equivalence-iff) says it must be.

:::
